_what: Model servers a person's other computers offer to this one (computer/offered-endpoints.mjs, asked after this computer's own servers by computer/local-models.mjs askLocal). The person keeps `sets` in `file`: each set is { id, label, offered_from, allowed_hosts, model, timeout_seconds? }, where `offered_from` is a text file (an https address or a path) listing one chat-completions address per line (# starts a comment). A line is accepted only if its scheme is in `schemes` and its host is one of the set's `allowed_hosts` (a name, or *.suffix); a set with none allows only `default_allowed_hosts`, this computer, so nothing leaves it until the person names another of their own computers. Accepted lines become rows tried in order after this computer's servers; the answer says which one served it (`served_by`) and the read's report says what each set offered, accepted and refused with the reason. `most_bytes` bounds the offered file, `fetch_seconds` how long it is waited for, `most_endpoints` how many lines a set may offer.

words.not_allowed: {host} is not one of the hosts you allowed
words.bad_scheme: {scheme} is not an address scheme this computer uses for models
words.too_many_lines: more than {most} addresses were offered; the rest are ignored
words.unreadable: the offered file could not be read: {why}
